title: Analysis of histone modifications in mouse neocortical neural progenitor-stem cells at various developmental stages
protocol: Kill pregnant ICR mice by cervical dislocation at E11 to E12.
Immerse the uterus in ice-cold DMEM-F12 containing 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Remove embryos from embryonic sacs one by one.
Transfer embryos to a 100-mm dish filled with ice-cold medium.
Hold down the head of each embryo with forceps and cut off the telencephalon with a scalpel.
Pull and tease apart the skin from the telencephalon and separate it from the brainstem.
Remove the vessel membrane (meninges) from the telencephalon.
Isolate the neocortex from the ventral telencephalon.
Collect the dissected neocortices into a 1.7-mL prelubricated microcentrifuge tube containing 500 μL of DMEM-F12 with 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Maintain the tube on ice until the neocortices settle to the bottom of the tube and then remove the medium.
Digest the neocortical tissue with Neuron Dissociation Solutions consisting of Enzyme solution, Dispersion solution, and Isolation solution.
Add 300 μL of Enzyme solution to the tissue and incubate for 20 min at 37°C.
Centrifuge the digest at 160 × g for 2 min at room temperature and remove the resulting supernatant.
Add 300 μL of Dispersion solution to the pellet and triturate gently with a 1-mL micropipette, taking care not to damage the cell suspension by pipetting too vigorously.
Add 300 μL of Isolation solution as a layer below the cell suspension.
Prepare DMEM-F12 supplemented with B-27, FGF2, and EGF.
Gently suspend the cell pellet in 4 mL of prewarmed DMEM-F12 containing supplements.
Count the number of isolated cells using a Neubauer hemocytometer.
Mix 10 μl of cell suspension with an equal volume of Trypan blue solution to assess viability under a microscope.
Collect 0.5 × 10^6 to 1.0 × 10^6 dissociated cells into a prelubricated microcentrifuge tube as neurogenic NPCs.
Add 0.1 volume of 11% formaldehyde solution dropwise to the cell suspension.
Rotate the tube for 10 minutes on a tube rotator.
Add 2.5 M glycine to achieve a final concentration of 125 mM in the cell suspension.
Centrifuge the mixture at 2,700 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the resulting supernatant.
Freeze the pellet in liquid nitrogen and store it at -80°C.
Culture dissociated cells at a density of 3.0 × 10^5 cells/mL in DMEM-F12 medium supplemented with B-27, FGF2, and EGF.
Transfer neurospheres to a 15-mL Falcon tube after culture for 3 days.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant.
Remove as much of the supernatant as possible after centrifugation.
Add 100 μL of DNase I solution into 4 mL of trypsin solution (final concentration 0.1 mg/mL).
Add 4 mL of trypsin solution containing DNase I to the neurosphere pellet.
Incubate the mixture for 10 min at 37°C.
Gently mix the suspension every 2–3 minutes with a 10-mL disposable pipette.
Add 40 μL of ovomucoid solution into 4 mL of aCSF (final concentration 0.7 mg/mL).
Add 4 mL of aCSF containing ovomucoid to the cell suspension from step 21.
Centrifuge the suspension at 200 × g for 2 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL of DMEM-F12 medium supplemented with B-27, FGF2, and EGF.
Mechanically dissociate the NPCs using a 10-mL disposable pipette by lightly pressing the tip against the bottom of the tube and pipetting at least 10 times.
Determine the cell number with a cell counting chamber.
Set aside 0.5 × 10^6 to 1.0 × 10^6 cells for ChIP analysis of NPCs in the neurogenic phase at 3 DIV.
Culture the remaining dissociated cells at a density of 3.0 × 10^5 cells/mL in DMEM-F12 medium supplemented with B-27, FGF2, and EGF.
Transfer 0.5 × 10^6 to 1.0 × 10^6 dissociated cells after culture for 9 DIV into a 1.7-mL prelubricated microcentrifuge tube for analysis as astrogliogenic NPCs.
Add 0.1 volume of 11% formaldehyde solution to the cell suspension to achieve a final concentration of 1%.
Rotate the tube on a tube rotator for 10 minutes.
Add 2.5 M glycine to the cell suspension to achieve a final concentration of 125 mM.
Centrifuge the mixture at 2,700 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the mixture.
Freeze the pellet in liquid nitrogen.
Store the frozen pellet at -80°C.
Resuspend protein A magnetic beads by vortex-mixing for >30 s.
Transfer a volume of beads corresponding to 20 μL (600 μg) of beads per ChIP reaction and 20 μL of beads per sample to a 1.7 mL prelubricated microcentrifuge tube.
Place the tube on the magnet to separate the beads from the solution.
Remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Swirl the beads gently until the solution becomes clear.
Attach a 27G injection needle to the tip of the aspirator to remove supernatant.
Wash the beads once with 250 μl of PBS containing 0.5% BSA by vortex-mixing or gentle tapping.
Incubate the tube on a tube rotator at approximately 5 rotations per minute for 1 h at 4°C.
Place the tube on the magnet to separate the beads from the solution and remove the supernatant.
Add 250 μl of PBS containing 0.5% BSA to the tube containing the beads.
Transfer beads for ChIP reaction into a new 1.7-mL prelubricated microcentrifuge tube.
Resuspend precipitated magnetic beads by pipetting.
Add PBS containing 0.5% BSA to the tube up to 250 μL.
Add 2 μg of antibodies to mouse IgMμ per ChIP reaction to the tube with blocked magnetic beads.
Incubate the tube on a tube rotator for >2 h at 4°C.
Place the tube on the magnet to separate the beads from the solution and remove the supernatant.
Wash anti-IgMμ–conjugated beads five times with 500 μL of Cell lysis buffer.
Resuspend the anti-IgMμ–conjugated beads in 250 μL of Cell lysis buffer.
Add 4 μg of antibodies to H2Aub per ChIP reaction to the beads.
Incubate the tube on a tube rotator overnight at 4°C (10–16 h).
Place the tube on the magnet to separate the beads from the solution and then remove the supernatant.
Wash the beads three times with 500 μL of cell lysis buffer.
Resuspend the beads by gentle rotation of the magnetic stand after each wash.
Resuspend the antibody-conjugated beads in 20 μL of Cell lysis buffer per ChIP reaction.
Pipette the bead suspension gently before transfer to tubes containing chromatin.
Incubate NPCs with 1 mL of swelling buffer per sample for 20 min on ice.
Centrifuge the tube at 5,800 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 150 μL of Cell lysis buffer.
Shear chromatin using a Hand Sonic UR-20P device with power setting “3” for 8 cycles (ON for 10 s, OFF for 20 s).
Increase power to “4” and continue shearing for 2 additional cycles (ON for 10 s, OFF for 20 s).
Run samples on an agarose gel electrophoresis to confirm appropriate chromatin length of 200–1000 base pairs.
Place the tube on ice during sonication to prevent temperature increase.
Centrifuge the tube at 20,380 × g for 5 min at 4°C if bubbling occurs.
Centrifuge the tube at 20,380 × g for 15 min at 4°C to remove cell debris.
Transfer all supernatant (~150 μL) to a new 1.7-mL prelubricated microcentrifuge tube.
Add 100 μL of Cell lysis buffer and 20 μL of blocked Dynabeads for preclearing from step 43 to the tube containing sheared chromatin.
Incubate the mixture on a tube rotator for 1 hour at 4°C.
Place the tube on the magnet to separate beads from solution.
Transfer 100 μL of supernatant to a new 1.7-mL prelubricated microcentrifuge tube for ChIP.
Transfer 50 μL of supernatant to another new tube for input determination and store at -20°C until reversal of cross-linking.
Add 150 μL of Cell lysis buffer to the tube containing supernatant for ChIP reaction.
Add 20 μL of anti-H2Aub-conjugated magnetic beads per ChIP to the chromatin extract.
Incubate the tube on a tube rotator overnight (10–16 h) at 4°C.
Place the tube on the magnet to separate the beads from the solution.
Remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Wash the beads six times with 500 μL of Cell lysis buffer.
Separate the beads on the magnetic stand, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the beads by agitation after each wash.
Wash the beads twice with 500 μL of Wash buffer A.
Separate the beads on the magnetic stand, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the beads by agitation after each wash.
Wash the beads twice with 500 μL of Wash buffer B.
Separate the beads on the magnetic stand, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the beads by agitation after each wash.
Wash the beads twice with 500 μL of TE buffer.
Separate the beads on the magnetic stand, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the beads by agitation after each wash.
Resuspend the beads in 200 μL of Elution buffer.
Proceed to step 71.
Thaw the tube containing the chromatin solution for determination of total input from step 61.
Add 150 μL of Elution buffer to the thawed tube.
Proceed to step 72.
Incubate the former tube at 65°C for 15 min, tapping and agitating every 2–3 min during incubation.
Add 5 μL of proteinase K solution to achieve a final enzyme concentration of 0.25 mg/mL.
Incubate overnight (10–16 h) at 37°C.
Transfer the tubes to a 65°C incubator for reversal of cross-linking and incubate for at least 6 h.
Add 200 μL of phenol–chloroform–isoamyl alcohol to each tube.
Shake vigorously.
Centrifuge at 20,380 × g for 15 min at room temperature.
Collect the resulting aqueous upper phase (~200 μL) and transfer it to a new prelubricated microcentrifuge tube.
Add 2.5 volumes of ethanol, 0.1 volume of 3 M sodium acetate, and 1 μL of glycogen (final concentration of 0.1 mg/mL).
Apply the tube to a vortex mixer.
Incubate at –20°C for 30 min.
Centrifuge at 20,380 × g for 15 min at room temperature.
Remove the resulting supernatant and wash the DNA pellet with 300 μL of 80% ethanol.
Allow the DNA pellet to dry in air.
Dissolve the DNA pellet in 50 μL of ddH2O.
Quantify H2Aub at target genes using qPCR.
Estimate relative binding frequency by calculating the percentage of total input recovered in the immunoprecipitate.
Use Neurog1, Fezf2, Lef1, and Tcfap2c as positive controls for neurogenic gene loci.
Use Actb and Gapdh as negative controls for housekeeping gene loci to verify H2Aub ChIP assay fidelity.
Calculate binding ratio of signals at target gene loci relative to those at negative gene loci.
Prepare a stock solution of forward primers in ddH2O at a final concentration of 10 μM.
Prepare a stock solution of reverse primers in ddH2O at a final concentration of 10 μM.
Combine 4.4 μL of ddH2O, 8 μL of THUNDERBIRD® SYBR® qPCR Mix, and 1.6 μL of primer stock solution per reaction for 1.1 times the desired number of reactions as a premixture.
Mix well by pipetting or tapping.
Assay samples at least in duplicate.
Generate a standard curve for the level of PCR amplification using purified genomic DNA of the input sample with the same premixture used for immunoprecipitated samples.
Cool a 96-well plate on a plate cooler.
Add 14 μL of the premixture to each well.
Add 2 μL of the purified DNA to each well.
Seal the plate with a seal compatible with qPCR.
Wipe the surface of the seal to remove dirty spots such as hand grease.
Vortex the plate briefly.
Centrifuge the plate at 100 × g for a few seconds at room temperature.
Perform the qPCR reaction with an appropriate program.
Check the protocol recommended by the product manufacturer for the precise qPCR program.
Include a melting curve analysis at the end of the program to confirm that only a single specific product was formed.
Redesign the qPCR primer set if two or more peaks are obtained in the melting curve analysis.
Calculate the relative concentration of the target DNA for all reactions for each primer pair using the corresponding standard curve.
Use the second derivative max method for calculation of the Cp (Ct) value.
Export the data to the “.txt” format.
Calculate the average of relative concentration of DNA for each sample from two or more replicates.
Correct the relative concentration value of each reaction by multiplying by the dilution factor.
Calculate the percent of input by dividing the value for each immunoprecipitate by that for its corresponding input.
